solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Do up catches around edges of fascia at the front

indicators.note: at the front puts the fascia letters before the turned-round catches
edges of takes only the outside letters of the word fascia
around here means the word for catches is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: to net something is to catch it, so catches gives NETS

explanation.surface: An instruction for fitting a car or shop front: secure it with clips round the fascia's edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches' looks like clasps but is the verb, as a fisherman nets fish; 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To do up a coat or a button is to fasten it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Go down with something bad following trip

indicators.note: following places the word for bad after the word for trip

parts.note: a trip is a stumble or fall
bad, as in feeling poorly, is ill

explanation.surface: Someone comes down sick with a bug after a stumble or a journey abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stops at 'something'; 'bad' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To go down with something is the idiom for catching an illness, which is what falling ill means.

clue.text: Very satisfied with half knocked back now and then

parts.note: very means so, as in so good
a need satisfied is one met

indicators.note: knocked back says the word for half is turned to read backwards

parts.note: semi- is the prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: Someone is only partly content, the other half of their satisfaction rejected, from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very satisfied' reads as one idea but splits into two words; 'knocked back' turns only the half word around.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening now and then occurs occasionally, which is the meaning of the adverb.

clue.text: Observing energies Yankee invested in golf

indicators.note: invested means the Yankee letter is put inside the pair standing for energies

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy, and the plural gives two of them
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone watches an American golfer pour energy into the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'energies' gives two Es, and 'invested' sets Y between them; the second 'in' is read as itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeing something means watching it closely, so it is a synonym for observing.

clue.text: Pretty down after former bridge partner's killed

indicators.note: after places the pretty-and-down part behind the former partner

parts.note: ex- means former, as in an ex-partner
in bridge the players are North, South, East and West, so a partner can be E for East
pretty means cute

explanation.surface: Someone is gloomy because their old bridge partner has been murdered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty down' reads as 'rather sad', but splits into CUTE and D.
explanation.definitionFit: A person executed has been put to death, so it is a synonym for killed.

clue.text: Ten are initially in line for diagnostic procedure

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the abbreviation for a railway line

parts.note: RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word are

explanation.surface: Ten people are queuing for a medical scan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives A from 'are', which goes inside RY.
explanation.definitionFit: An X-ray image is used by doctors to look inside the body, a standard diagnostic procedure.

clue.text: Tory immorality includes number with influence

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: includes means the word for immorality takes the number's letter inside it

parts.note: vice is immorality

explanation.surface: A Conservative's moral failings go hand in hand with buying votes and power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts N inside VICE to make VINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To convince someone is to bring them round to a view, a way to influence them.

clue.text: Bottom of dress encircled by musical note motif

indicators.note: encircled by means the hem sits inside the letters for the musical note

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale
the hem is the bottom edge of a dress

explanation.surface: A dress has a musical note pattern running round its hem.
explanation.walkthrough: Te (or ti) is the seventh note of do-re-mi; 'encircled by' wraps it round the dress's bottom edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring idea in a work of art or music, in other words a theme.

clue.text: Lido resort's keeping PH neutral for sea creature

indicators.note: keeping means the rearranged letters hold the two letters inside them
resort here is a verb, to sort again, so the letters of lido are rearranged

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for neutral, as on a gear lever

explanation.surface: A seaside lido keeps its pool water at neutral pH for the visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort's' is 'resort is', resort as a verb (sort again), the anagram signal; 'keeping' puts PH inside the result before N is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a marine mammal, one example of a creature living in the sea.

clue.text: Permit to catch urchin and sea snail

indicators.note: to catch means the word for permit holds the urchin's word inside it

parts.note: to let is to permit
an imp is a mischievous child, an urchin

explanation.surface: A licence to collect sea urchins and sea snails on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'urchin' looks like the spiny sea creature but means a scamp; 'to catch' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet is a marine gastropod clinging to rocks, broadly a kind of sea snail.

clue.text: Mother and I, eating at home, take on a large dinner

indicators.note: take on means the following letters are added at the end
eating means the mother-and-me letters swallow the at-home letters

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
I, the speaker, becomes me
to be in is to be at home
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Mother and I, dining in, tackle a huge dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' must become its object form to fit; 'eating' signals the insertion and 'take on' adds the rest at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The main meal of the day is the principal one, which in many homes is called dinner.

clue.text: Rally floating voter after general election starts

indicators.note: after places the rearranged voter letters behind the starting letters
starts takes the opening letter of general and of election
floating suggests letters drifting loose, so voter is rearranged

explanation.surface: A rally to win over floating voters after a general election is called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floating' turns VOTER into TOVER; 'starts' gives GE from 'general election'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to recover from illness or a setback, and to get over something is to recover from it.

clue.text: Fiancé gets back tax taken care of

indicators.note: back means the letters for the tax are read in reverse

parts.note: NI is National Insurance, a UK tax on earnings
tended means looked after or taken care of

explanation.surface: A fiancé gets a tax refund sorted out for them.
explanation.walkthrough: National Insurance (NI) is a deduction from British pay packets; 'back' turns it to IN.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is the person one is engaged to marry, a slightly old-fashioned word for a fiancé.

clue.text: Hard trailing strike on City that's electronically sophisticated

indicators.note: trailing means the hard letter comes behind the rest

parts.note: to strike is to hit
EC is the London postcode for the City of London
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A hard-hitting strike on the City's financial systems by tech-savvy attackers.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC; 'trailing' puts the hard letter last, and 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: High-tech describes advanced technology, typically electronic, so it fits sophisticated gadgetry.

clue.text: Nervous using jack thing with burst tyre

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
it can stand for a thing

indicators.note: burst means the letters of tyre are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorist is anxious changing a punctured tyre with a jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jack' looks like the car-lifting tool but is the playing card; 'burst' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone jittery is jumpy and on edge, in other words nervous.

clue.text: Clam bakes do contain some meat

indicators.note: contain says the answer sits inside the run of letters in the words before

explanation.surface: Clam bakes, the seafood feasts, do include a bit of meat too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' belongs with 'meat' as the definition, not with the hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb is the flesh of a young sheep, one kind of meat.

clue.text: Perhaps Leo is dozing, miserably nursing a cold

indicators.note: nursing means the rearranged letters hold the a-and-cold letters inside
miserably signals the letters of is and dozing are put in a wretched new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Leo the lion snoozes, unhappily coddling a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leo is' reads as the subject, but 'is' joins 'dozing' as fodder; 'miserably' scrambles them and 'nursing' holds A and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is one of the twelve star signs, so it is an example, flagged by perhaps.

clue.text: Beset by problems, popular choice tucking into beer

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: tucking into means the word for choice goes inside the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a pick is a choice, as in take your pick

explanation.surface: A popular pick ends up down a pint, with trouble following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' sounds like eating but signals one piece going inside the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a pickle is an idiom for being in a difficult situation.

clue.text: Picked up new significance surrounding memorial

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for significance goes round the other part

parts.note: moment means importance or significance, as in of great moment

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: new sounds like nu, the Greek letter

explanation.surface: A memorial is noticed to take on new meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' means heard: the Greek letter nu sounds like 'new'; 'surrounding' wraps the significance word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument is a structure built to commemorate someone, which is what a memorial is.

clue.text: Fraud detective embarrassed over shambolic notes

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: over means the embarrassed word spreads across the jumbled notes, covering them

parts.note: shy means bashful or embarrassed

indicators.note: shambolic means chaotic, so the letters of notes are jumbled

explanation.surface: A detective is red-faced after making a mess of the banknotes in a fraud case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shambolic' scrambles the notes, and 'over' lays the embarrassed word across them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraud is deception for gain, and dishonesty is the quality behind it, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: State cleared criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of cleared are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: The state clears a criminal of the charges.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something is to say it formally, to announce or declare it.

clue.text: Friendly women's section

parts.note: an arm is a branch or section of an organisation

explanation.surface: A sociable women's branch of a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm welcome is a friendly one, so warm is a synonym when describing people.

clue.text: Schooner finally given free rein under master seaman

indicators.note: under means the following letters sit below the master's letters in this down answer

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of schooner
free means the letters of rein are loosed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A schooner's master hands over the reins at last, letting the crew sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R from 'Schooner'; 'free' turns REIN into INER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a sailor, so the word is a synonym for seaman.

clue.text: Zones out, nothing's interrupting sleep

indicators.note: interrupting means the letter for nothing breaks into the rearranged letters
out signals that the letters of zones are put out of order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone zones out, nothing disturbing their nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns ZONES into SNOZE, and 'interrupting' puts O after SNO.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooze is a short light sleep, a doze.

clue.text: Sample of classic liqueur for exclusive little group

indicators.note: Sample of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A taster of a classic liqueur is offered to a select few.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'for', but that is a link word: 'for exclusive little group' cannot stand in for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique is a small close-knit set of people who keep others out.

clue.text: Furious with current pay

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a rate is a rate of pay

explanation.surface: Workers are livid about their present wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' reads as 'present' but is the physics symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, a direct synonym for furious.

clue.text: Borderline F's concerning in reading level

parts.note: the letter F is taken as written

indicators.note: in places the word for concerning inside the reading-and-level letters

parts.note: R stands for reading, one of the three Rs
a tier is a level or layer
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A school report: an F grade in reading puts a pupil on the borderline of a level.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading, writing and arithmetic are 'the three Rs', so reading gives R; 'in' places the concerning word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is the line where two countries meet, a border line.

clue.text: Leading man's immersed in the role

indicators.note: immersed in says the answer is sunk inside the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: An actor playing the lead is absorbed in the part.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of a story or film is its principal male character, so leading man fits.

clue.text: Stimulated a wide advanced knowledge with education

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide ball
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
ken is range of knowledge, as in beyond one's ken

explanation.surface: Someone was fired up by a broad, sophisticated grasp of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, marked W.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awakened has been roused or stirred into activity, a sense close to stimulated.

clue.text: Throw away bag for ordinary double knit needle

indicators.note: bag means to enclose, so the bin letters hold the others inside

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away
D is the abbreviation for double, as in darts scoring
K is the abbreviation for knit in knitting patterns

explanation.surface: A knitter discards a bag of plain double-knit wool and its needle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bag' reads as a noun but is a verb meaning to enclose: BIN takes ODK inside after B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodkin is a blunt thick needle with a large eye, used for threading tape or ribbon.

clue.text: Help centre with distribution of notice for poll

indicators.note: centre takes the middle letters of the word help
distribution of signals the letters of notice are spread out in a new order

explanation.surface: A help centre hands out leaflets about a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' gives EL from 'Help'; 'distribution of' turns NOTICE into ECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A poll is a vote held to choose representatives, which is what an election is.

clue.text: More discovered about extra-terrestrial rock

indicators.note: discovered about suggests letters strewn around, so those of more and the alien are rearranged

parts.note: ET is short for extra-terrestrial, as in the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: More was found out about a rock from space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extra-terrestrial rock' looks like the definition, but 'extra-terrestrial' gives ET, mixed with MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a piece of rock or metal from space burning up in the atmosphere.
